                               PETITION FOR REVIEW
      Pursuant to Section 313(b) of the Federal Power Act ("FPA"), 16 U.S.C.

Section 8251(b), Federal Rule of Appellate Procedure 15, and District of Columbia

Circuit Rule 15, the Pennsylvania Office of Consumer Advocate ("PA OCA")

respectfully petitions this Court to review the following Orders of the Federal Energy

Regulatory Commission ("Commission"):


      • Order Conditionally Authorizing Merger and Disposition of
        Jurisdictional Facilities, Constellation Energy Corp., Docket No.
        EC25-43-000, 192 FERC ¶ 61,074 (July 23, 2025) ("Merger
        Authorization Order") (attached hereto as Exhibit A); and
       • Notice of Denial of Rehearing by Operation of Law and Providing
        for Further Consideration, Constellation Energy Corp., Docket No.
        EC25-43-001, 192 FERC ¶ 62,183 (Sep. 22, 2025) ("Denial
        Notice") (attached hereto as Exhibit B).

      This Court has jurisdiction pursuant to 16 U.S.C. Section 8251(b). The PA

OCA is aggrieved by the Merger Authorization Order and the Denial Notice, was an

active participant in the underlying Commission proceedings below, and now seeks

review of the Merger Authorization Order and the Denial Notice through this

Petition.

      More specifically, the PA OCA is a Pennsylvania state agency charged with

representing the interests of Pennsylvania utility consumers in proceedings before

the Commission and federal courts in connection with any matter involving

Commission regulation that affects Pennsylvania ratepayers. 71 P.S. § 309-4. The

PA OCA timely intervened in the Commission proceeding below on February 25,

2025. The PA OCA also filed a Protest, Motion for Leave to Answer and Answer,

Motion for Leave to Submit Comments and Comments, and Comments regarding

the Settlement Agreement. The PA OCA requested the Commission to examine the

impact of the application, seeking authorization for a transaction through which

Constellation Energy Corporation and Constellation Energy Generation, LLC will

acquire Calpine Corporation, including its subsidiaries ("Proposed Transaction"), on

Pennsylvania consumers.
         In the Merger Authorization Order, the Commission granted the PA OCA's
                          •,
intervention and accepted the submission of the PA OCA's pleadings. Merger

Authorization Order ¶¶ 14, 15, 20, 36, 42, 44, 45. However, the Commission

declined to examine the impact of the Proposed Transaction on the Pennsylvania

retail electricity markets and default service supply process because the

Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission had not requested that the Commission do

so. Merger Authorization Order ¶¶ 190-193

        The PA OCA filed a timely request for rehearing of the Merger Authorization

Order on August 22, 2025. On September 22, 2025, the Commission issued the

Denial Notice, stating: "In the absence of Commission action on a request for

rehearing within 30 .days from the date it is filed, the request for rehearing may be

deemed to have been denied." Denial Notice at 1.'

        b.     Description of the Proposed Transaction

11. Applicants state that, pursuant to the Proposed Transaction, the Constellation
Applicants will acquire the Calpine Applicants." As a result of the closing of the
Proposed Transaction, Applicants state that Calpine and the Calpine Public Utility
Subsidiaries will be indirect wholly owned subsidiaries of Constellation, and Calpine's
existing upstream owners, ECP and AI Holdings, will each hold less than 10% of the
voting equity interests in Constellation and will not have any right to appoint a board
member to the boards of Constellation or any of its subsidiaries. According to
Applicants, post-closing of the Proposed Transaction, neither ECP nor AI Holdings will
be affiliated with the Constellation Applicants or the Calpine Applicants."

a non-utility associate company' or the pledge-of enctunbrance of utility assets for the
benefit of an associate company, unless the Commission determines that the cross-
subsidization, pledge, or encumbrance will be consistent with the public interest."29 The
